results.judge_explanation: The diagnosis identifies the undeclared var.env reference in main.tf and its suggested fix restores var.environment, which matches the answer key; the 'rename declaration' note is only a conditional next check, not the primary recommendation.

diagnosis.root_cause: Commit b7565223 changed the locals block in sample-app/infra/main.tf to reference `var.env`, but the only declared variable is `environment`, so `terraform validate` fails with 'Reference to undeclared input variable'.
key_evidence: [10:53:24] Error: Reference to undeclared input variable
[10:53:24] An input variable with the name "env" has not been declared. This variable
diagnosis.suggested_fix: In sample-app/infra/main.tf line 12, restore the reference to the declared variable: `app_name = "calculator-${var.environment}"`.
assumptions: The branch's copy of main.tf was not read in full (`git show fail/bad-terraform:sample-app/infra/main.tf` was not run). The git-investigator concluded that `variable "environment"` is still declared there, and no `variable "env"` exists, from a diff that changed only one line.
The rename to `env` was not meant to come with a renamed variable declaration. The commit changed only the reference, so restoring it is the safer fix.
next_checks: Run `git show fail/bad-terraform:sample-app/infra/main.tf` and confirm only `variable "environment"` is declared.
After the fix, run `terraform fmt -check && terraform init -input=false && terraform validate` in sample-app/infra locally.
If the shorter name `env` is actually wanted, rename the variable declaration as well and check that nothing else sets `environment` (TF_VAR_environment, tfvars files).

results.judge_explanation: The diagnosis identifies subtract() returning a + b instead of a - b as the cause of the test_subtract failure (14 vs 6), and its fix restores 'return a - b' while leaving the test unchanged, matching the answer key.

diagnosis.root_cause: Commit 4446cb4 ('Refactor calculator arithmetic helpers') changed subtract() in sample-app/app/calculator.py from `return a - b` to `return a + b`, so subtract(10, 4) returns 14 instead of 6 and test_subtract fails.
diagnosis.suggested_fix: In sample-app/app/calculator.py, change subtract() back to `return a - b`, as it is on main. Leave tests/test_calculator.py unchanged.
assumptions: The operator flip was an accidental regression, not an intended behavior change; the commit message calls it a refactor.
next_checks: Run `python -m pytest -v` in sample-app with the fix applied and confirm all 5 tests pass.
Ask the author of commit 4446cb4 whether changing subtract's behavior was intended.
Look for any other code that calls subtract() and may have been changed to rely on the new behavior.

results.judge_explanation: The diagnosis identifies the missing 'deploy-token' credential in Jenkins as the cause, calls the README unrelated, and suggests re-creating the credential with no code changes, which matches the answer key.

diagnosis.root_cause: The Jenkins credential store has no Secret-text credential with ID 'deploy-token' that the calculator job can use, so withCredentials failed when the Deploy stage started. The branch's only change, a README, is unrelated.
key_evidence: ERROR: Could not find credentials entry with ID 'deploy-token'
diagnosis.suggested_fix: In Jenkins (Manage Jenkins > Credentials), create or restore a credential of kind 'Secret text' with ID exactly 'deploy-token', in a scope the calculator multibranch job can read (for example global, or the job's folder). Then rebuild the branch. Leave the Jenkinsfile and the README as they are.
assumptions: The credential was deleted, renamed, re-scoped or saved as the wrong type in Jenkins. The Jenkins credential store itself was not inspected, because the investigation is read-only.
The diagnosis comes from the saved console log, not a live fetch from Jenkins, so the current Jenkins state may differ.
next_checks: Check that a credential with ID 'deploy-token' exists under Manage Jenkins > Credentials and is of kind 'Secret text'.
Check that its scope (global or folder) and domain make it visible to the calculator multibranch job.
Check whether main's latest build also fails at Deploy, which would show the credential is missing for every branch.
Check the Jenkins audit or config history for when 'deploy-token' was removed or changed.

results.judge_explanation: The diagnosis identifies the misspelled credentialsId 'deploy-tokn' and proposes changing it back to 'deploy-token' in the Jenkinsfile, which matches the answer key; the conditional next-check about creating a credential under an intended ID is not the primary fix.

diagnosis.root_cause: Commit 4a1b8a2 on fail/missing-credential changed the Deploy stage's credentialsId from 'deploy-token' to the misspelled 'deploy-tokn'. No Jenkins credential has that ID, so withCredentials failed before the sh step ran.
key_evidence: ERROR: Could not find credentials entry with ID 'deploy-tokn'
diagnosis.suggested_fix: In sample-app/Jenkinsfile (Deploy stage, about line 60), change credentialsId back from 'deploy-tokn' to 'deploy-token', which is the ID main uses.
assumptions: A Jenkins credential with ID 'deploy-token' exists, because main builds green with it. The Jenkins credential store itself was not checked.
next_checks: In Manage Jenkins > Credentials, confirm that a Secret text credential with ID 'deploy-token' exists and is in scope for the calculator job.
Check whether the commit was meant to switch to a different credential on purpose. If so, create that credential in Jenkins under the intended ID instead of reverting.
After the fix, confirm that the Deploy stage passes and prints the token length.

results.judge_explanation: The diagnosis identifies the 3s→90s default change exceeding the 1-minute stage timeout, and its primary fix restores the default to 3s, matching the answer key; the secondary advice to raise the timeout for slower environments is an acceptable fix, not a wrong one.

diagnosis.root_cause: Commit 220b4ad on fail/timeout raised the default smoke-test wait in sample-app/scripts/smoke_test.py from 3s to 90s, but the unchanged Smoke Test stage has a 1-minute timeout, so Jenkins stopped the script at 60s and aborted the build.
key_evidence: [10:54:12] Timeout set to expire in 1 min 0 sec
[10:54:13] Waiting 90s for the service to become healthy...
[10:55:12] Cancelling nested steps due to timeout
diagnosis.suggested_fix: In sample-app/scripts/smoke_test.py, set the default back to WAIT_SECONDS = int(os.environ.get("SMOKE_WAIT_SECONDS", "3")), as on main. Slower environments that need a longer wait should set SMOKE_WAIT_SECONDS for their run and raise the Smoke Test stage timeout to match, rather than changing the default for every environment.
assumptions: I assume main's 3s default passes the Smoke Test stage on this Jenkins; no main build log was checked.
I don't know whether the script waits a fixed time or stops once the service is healthy; the script body was not read beyond the changed line.
No report identified which slower environment the commit was meant for, or whether it really needs 90s.
next_checks: Check that the latest main build's Smoke Test stage passed with the 3s default.
Read smoke_test.py to see whether WAIT_SECONDS is a fixed sleep or an upper limit on health polling.
Ask the commit author which environment needed a longer wait, and make sure that environment sets SMOKE_WAIT_SECONDS and a stage timeout comfortably longer than the wait.
The Test stage was slow (pytest took 90.55s, with a gap during collection from 10:52:32 to 10:54:09) but passed; keep an eye on it against the 10-minute pipeline timeout.
